newsitem.title: BULGARIA: World Bank agrees heating meters loan to Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: World Bank agrees heating meters loan to Bulgaria.

text.p: The World Bank on Wednesday concluded negotiations with Bulgaria to transfer $12 million from an existing loan to a pilot project to supply 18,000 heating meters throughout the country.
The energy ministry will use the cash from a $98 million loan extended to the construction ministry last year for the modernisation of the water system.

Heating meters will be distributed to 15 district heating firms and about 17 percent of Bulgarians are customers of these firms and would benefit either directly or indirectly from the project, a World Bank statement said.
People who up to now have paid a flat rate for their heating will be able to pay according to consumption.

Heating was heavily subsidised during the communist era but soaring prices mean Bulgarians are keen to save power this winter. More than 12 percent of Bulgarians whose homes are linked to central heating have asked for supply to be reduced.
"The first deliveries and installation of heating meters is expected to take place in summer 1997," the World Bank said.

Energy officials said the project would be implemented in two years. They said another project for supplying individual heating meters in households will be funded by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the European Union's Phare programme.
